question.text: Two plane mirrors are inclined to each other such that a ray of light incident on the first mirror <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> and parallel to the second mirror <math><mo>(</mo><msub><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></math> is finally reflected from the second mirror <math><mo>(</mo><msub><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></math> and parallel to the first mirror <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> The angle between the two mirrors will be:

solution.text:
As given in question AB||CO

∴∠ABF=θ

From laws of reflection

∠OBC=θ

Similarly CD‖OB
